([[Lincolnton, North Carolina]]) | draft_year = 2024 | career_start = 2023 | years1 = 2023–2024 | team1 = [[Adelaide 36ers]] | years2 = {{nbay|2024|full=y}} | team2 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team3 = →[[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] | years4 = {{nbay|2025|full=y}} | team4 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | years5 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team5 = →[[Windy City Bulls]] | years6 = 2026–present | team6 = [[Brampton Honey Badgers]] | highlights = }} '''Trentyn Levi Flowers''' (born March 8, 2005) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Brampton Honey Badgers]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL). ==High school career== Flowers played his freshman season at [[Jackson County Comprehensive High School]] in [[Jefferson, Georgia]], where he received his first [[NCAA Division I]] basketball scholarship offer in 2021.{{cite web |last1=Dennis |first1=Ryne |title=Local freshman gets first Division I offer from former UGA basketball player Jonas Hayes |url=https://www.onlineathens.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2021/02/10/xavier-basketball-offers-jackson-county-freshman-trentyn-flowers/4451166001/ |website=Athens Banner-Herald |access-date=September 15, 2023 |date=February 10, 2021}} He moved to [[Huntington Prep School]] in [[Huntington, West Virginia]], for his sophomore season and garnered continued collegiate attention for his ball-handling skills and "big guard" playing style.{{cite web |last1=Fowler |first1=Chapel |title=6-foot-8 point guard calls himself a 'unicorn.' Where does he stand with UNC basketball? |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2022/01/07/north-carolina-tar-heels-unc-basketball-recruiting-2024-trentyn-flowers-6-foot-8-point-guard-recruit/9077268002/ |website=The Fayetteville Observer |access-date=September 15, 2023 |date=January 7, 2022}} Flowers transferred to [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Los Angeles, California]], midway through his sophomore season.{{cite web |last1=London |first1=Dushawn |title=No. 6 prospect in the class of 2024 Trentyn Flowers updates recruitment Flowers also briefly attended Mission Viejo High School at the end of his sophomore season before moving to Combine Academy |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Basketball-recruiting-UCLA-USC-Michigan-Trentyn-Flowers-247Sports-183448041/ |website=247 Sports |access-date=September 15, 2023 |date=February 26, 2022}} He transferred to Combine Academy in [[Lincolnton, North Carolina]], in 2022.{{cite web |last1=Cassidy |first1=Rob |title=Trentyn Flowers talks potential visits, upcoming trimming of list |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/trentyn-flowers-talks-potential-visits-upcoming-trimming-of-list |website=Rivals |access-date=September 15, 2023 |date=November 29, 2022}} Flowers was considered as a top-10 [[small forward]] in the class of 2024.{{cite web |last1=Holton |first1=Brooks |title=Kenny Payne lands 3rd high-profile commitment; Trentyn Flowers picks Louisville basketball |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/recruiting/2023/03/17/louisville-basketball-recruiting-trentyn-flowers-picks-kenny-payne/69990782007/ |website=Louisville Courier Journal |access-date=September 15, 2023 |date=March 22, 2023}} On March 17, 2023, he declared his commitment to join the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]] and would reclassify to the class of 2023 to be eligible for the 2023–24 season. ==Professional career== ===Adelaide 36ers (2023–2024)=== On August 14, 2023, Flowers announced that he had decommitted from Louisville to sign with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) as a member of the league's Next Stars program.{{cite web|first=Dale|last=Fletcher|title=Trentyn Flowers signs on as NBL Next Star at 36ers.|url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/next-star-flowers-joins-36ers-for-nbl24|website=Adelaide36ers.com|date=August 14, 2023|access-date=September 15, 2023}}{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|title=Trentyn Flowers leaving Louisville for Australia's NBL|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/38193022/trentyn-flowers-leaving-louisville-australia-nbl|website=ESPN.com|date=August 15, 2023|access-date=September 15, 2023}} He stated that he wanted to play at the [[point guard]] position and named former NBL players [[LaMelo Ball]] and [[Josh Giddey]] as motivations. On August 27, 36ers head coach [[C. J. Bruton]] named Flowers as the starting point guard for the team.{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Woods|title=Adelaide's Next Star-ter|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/adelaide-s-next-star-ter|website=NBL.com.au|date=August 27, 2023|access-date=September 15, 2023}} After attempts at using Flowers as a point guard to begin the preseason, the 36ers moved him to a [[swingman|wing forward]] position.{{cite web|first=Olgun|last=Uluc|title=Sources: Adelaide 36ers to release import|url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/38443272/nbl-sources-adelaide-36ers-release-import|website=ESPN.com|date=September 20, 2023|access-date=September 20, 2023}}{{cite web|title=Failed experiment: Adelaide 36ers shift teen point guard|url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/basketball/nbl2024-adelaide-36ers-abandon-trentyn-flowers-point-guard-experiment/news-story/7cf8fe7b351dea614469bba58f8a04b3|website=AdelaideNow.com|date=September 20, 2023|access-date=December 28, 2023}} Flowers made his debut off the bench in a loss to the [[Brisbane Bullets]] on September 29, 2023, and recorded four points and five rebounds.{{cite web|title=Bullets fire after early NBL wobbles to beat 36ers|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bullets-fire-after-early-nbl-wobbles-to-beat-36ers|website=NBL.com.au|date=September 29, 2023|access-date=September 29, 2023}} He scored 23 points, including 18 in the fourth quarter, to lead the 36ers to their first win of the season against the [[Illawarra Hawks]] on October 14, 2023.{{cite web|title=Flowers explodes as Sixers open NBL24 account|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/flowers-explodes-as-sixers-open-nbl24-account|website=NBL.com.au|date=October 14, 2023|access-date=October 14, 2023}} Flowers returned to the 36ers' starting line-up after [[Scott Ninnis]] took over as head coach from Bruton in December 2023.{{cite web|first=Dale|last=Fletcher|title=Humphries, Vasiljevic, Kell and Wiley fire but 36ers go down 116-101|url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com.au/news/sixers-show-fight-but-fall-to-fast-finishing-taipans|website=Adelaide36ers.com.au|date=December 9, 2023|access-date=December 12, 2023}} He injured his knee in January 2024,{{cite web|title=Flowers a game-time decision against Kings|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/flowers-a-game-time-decision-against-kings|website=NBL.com.au|date=January 10, 2024|access-date=February 20, 2024}} and subsequently fell out of the playing rotation.{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Woods|title=Next Stars Wrap - Round 18, NBL24|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/next-stars-wrap-round-18-nbl24|website=NBL.com.au|date=February 5, 2024|access-date=February 20, 2024}} Flowers then suffered from a neck strain,{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Woods|title=Next Stars Wrap - Round 19, NBL24|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/next-stars-wrap-round-19-nbl24|website=NBL.com.au|date=February 12, 2024|access-date=February 20, 2024}} and missed the last two rounds of the season.{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Woods|title=Next Stars Wrap - Round 20, NBL24|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/next-stars-wrap-round-20-nbl24 |website=NBL.com.au|date=February 19, 2024|access-date=February 20, 2024}} Flowers appeared in 18 games with the 36ers and averaged 5.2 points per game. ===Los Angeles / San Diego Clippers (2024–2025)=== On April 14, 2024, Flowers declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Flowers declares for NBA Draft|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/flowers-declares-for-nba-draft|website=NBL.com.au|date=April 14, 2024|access-date=April 20, 2024}} He was invited to participate in the [[NBA draft combine]].{{cite web|title=Flowers invited to NBA Draft Combine|url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/flowers-invited-to-nba-draft-combine|website=Adelaide36ers.com|date=May 7, 2024|access-date=May 24, 2024}} After going unselected in the draft, Flowers signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] on July 25.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Clippers Sign Trentyn Flowers To Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/clippers-sign-trentyn-flowers-to-two-way-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 25, 2024|access-date=July 25, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Brooks|last=Holton|title=Trentyn Flowers, former Louisville basketball signee, joins Los Angeles Clippers|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2024/06/28/trentyn-flowers-los-angeles-clippers-nba-draft-2024-louisville-basketball/73899246007/|website=Courier-Journal.com|date=June 28, 2024|access-date=June 29, 2024}} On September 25, he was ruled out of participating in Clippers training camp after he underwent surgery on his left wrist.{{cite web |title=Clippers' Trentyn Flowers: Out for training camp |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-trentyn-flowers-out-for-training-camp/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=October 1, 2024 |date=September 25, 2024}} Flowers appeared in six games for the Clippers during the 2024–25 season and averaged 1.8 points per game.{{cite web |title=Clippers' Trentyn Flowers: Plays six games in 2024-25 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-trentyn-flowers-plays-six-games-in-2024-25/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=May 10, 2025}} He spent the majority of the season with the San Diego Clippers in the NBA G League where he averaged 17.7 points, 5.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 40 games. On October 14, 2025, Flowers was waived by Los Angeles.{{Cite web|title=Clippers officially cut ties with 6-foot-7 forward, skilled G-League scoring threat|url=https://www.mlbdraftleague.com/west-virginia/news/2025-coaching-staff|access-date=November 18, 2025|website=ca.sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} ===Chicago / Windy City Bulls (2025–2026)=== On October 17, 2025, Flowers signed a two-way contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2025 |title=Bulls sign Trentyn Flowers to two-way contract |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-trentyn-flowers-to-two-way-contract |access-date=October 24, 2025 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} He made two appearances for the Bulls, recording averages of 2.0 points, 0.5 rebounds, and 0.5 assists. Flowers was waived by Chicago on January 6, 2026.{{Cite web |last=Baltes |first=Mack |date=2026-01-07 |title=Yuki Kawamura’s path to playing time after signing with Bulls|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/yuki-kawamuras-path-playing-time-003515300.html |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=Yahoo Sports / The Sporting News |language=en-US }}{{Cite web |last=RotoWire Staff |first= |date=2026-03-05 |title=Bulls’ Yuki Kawamura: Inks two‑way pact with Chicago |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bulls-yuki-kawamura-inks-two-way-pact-with-chicago/ |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=CBS Sports |language=en-US }}{{Cite web |title=Bulls Sign Yuki Kawamura To Two‑Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-yuki-kawamura-to-two-way-contract-2 |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=NBA.com |language=en-US }} === Brampton Honey Badgers === On July 1, 2026, Flowers signed with the [[Brampton Honey Badgers]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]]. He made his Brampton debut the following day, scoring 22 points in an 81–76 victory over the [[Ottawa BlackJacks]].{{cite web |title=Trentyn Flowers scores 22 points in CEBL debut as Honey Badgers beat BlackJacks |url=https://www.cbc.ca/player/play/video/9.7257010 |website=cbc.ca |publisher=[[CBC Sports]]}}{{cite web |title=Brampton Honey Badgers Sign NBA Forward Flowers |url=https://www.cebl.ca/brampton-honey-badgers-sign-nba-forward-flowers |website=cebl.ca |publisher=Canadian Elite Basketball League}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2024}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
